title: Inside the Earth: Volcanoes and Earthquakes
summary: Look at the layers of the Earth and see why the ground shakes and volcanoes erupt.

steps.title: Layers of the Earth
sentences: Earth has four main layers: the crust, the mantle, the outer core and the inner core.
The crust is the thin rocky skin we live on.
Under it the mantle is hot, thick rock that moves very slowly, and at the centre the core is mostly iron and nickel.

steps.title: Moving plates
sentences: The crust is broken into huge pieces called tectonic plates.
They float on the mantle and move a few centimetres every year, about as fast as your fingernails grow.
Where plates meet, they can push together, pull apart or slide past each other.

steps.title: Earthquakes
sentences: Plates sometimes stick against each other as they try to move.
When the stress becomes too much, the rock suddenly slips and sends out shaking waves.
That sudden slip is an earthquake, and scientists measure its strength with a seismograph.

steps.title: Volcanoes
sentences: A volcano is an opening where melted rock called magma rises up from below.
Once it reaches the surface it is called lava.
Many volcanoes lie along the edges of plates, including the famous Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean.

facts: The Himalayas are still growing taller by a few millimetres a year because India's plate keeps pushing into Asia.
The deepest hole humans have drilled is about 12 kilometres, which is less than one half of one percent of the way to the centre.
Some volcanoes erupt under the sea.

quiz.q: What are the main layers of the Earth in order from the top?
quiz.why: From the outside in: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.

quiz.q: What is melted rock called after it reaches the surface?
quiz.why: Underground it is magma, and on the surface it is lava.

quiz.q: What is the cause of most earthquakes?
options: Sudden slipping of rock along a fault
quiz.why: Rocks slip suddenly when stress builds along plate edges.
